correctness.rationale: The sharp expected squared-error identity and congruence reduce the normalized Kaczmarz optimization exactly to a diagonal-majorant SDP. Explicit dual correlations and primal diagonals agree in objective. For t<=1/(n-1) the sharp path Cauchy-Schwarz inequality proves global PSD; for t> the strictly positive Dirichlet interior block and exactly cancelling boundary Schur complement prove global PSD. Monotonicity of sin(theta)/sin((n-1)theta) gives a unique root. Complementary slackness proves unique probabilities, including at the threshold; an implicit-function argument establishes nonempty normalized systems. A standalone standard-library checker passed 3,060 supporting assertion groups on 56 examples, not relied upon for an infinite proof. Scope excludes multistep/adaptive/rectangular systems.

originality.rationale: The checked Kaczmarz sources give general rate and optimization methods without evaluating the stated all-dimension inverse-Gram signed cycle. Effective-resistance theory settles the weak-edge definiteness threshold but not the supercritical semidefinite optimum. General cycle-elliptope completion describes feasible correlations rather than this unique sampling law. A four-variable special case is excluded and cannot immediately imply the n>=5 nonconstant Dirichlet interpolation. Original primary cycle-completion and some specialist optimal-sampling sources were unavailable in full, and their possible stronger implications remain genuine historical risks.
residual_risks: A previously solved weighted signed planar-spin ring may imply the correlation optimum under an equivalence not fully inspected.
The 1993 original cycle-completion paper and an analogous 1986 frustrated-spin paper were not accessible in full.
Other unindexed specialist papers could already solve the exact weighted-elliptope maximization.
An older exact four-variable special case is excluded from the new all-dimensional claim; the claimed novelty is the n>=5 formula and global Dirichlet proof.

value.rationale: The sharp fixed-iid one-step Kaczmarz contraction is a motivated natural solver invariant; row correlations with one antagonistic closing edge are a tractable but nontrivial signed sparse model. The result replaces a generic SDP with explicit unique all-n>=5 probabilities, sharp dimension-dependent threshold and rigorous rank-two optimality certificates. The sine-ratio and positive Dirichlet interpolation are not a routine substitution into the previously known four-variable case. The theorem does not claim downstream or multistep results.
